tasks.short: Check and correct completed program logs

steps.what: Select completed program logs and specify applicable accuracy and conformance checks
Check recorded program times, identifiers and explicit conformance totals against specified rules
Resolve program log inaccuracies and accept corrections and conformance conclusions

tasks.design: Configure explicit completed-log checks in {OTHER}, the broadcast scheduling and logging system, and retain a source-linked discrepancy list. The director resolves ambiguous records and signs corrections; the checks cannot establish legal compliance on their own.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated comparisons of log entries and fixed rule totals consumed manual checking time.
tasks.enabler_now: Broadcast scheduling software can check explicit content rules and repeat limits; native completed-log checks should be tested before custom code.
tasks.still_hard: Programme classification, applicable rules and the reason for an unusual log entry require human assessment.
tasks.human_edge: The director distinguishes a recording defect from a substantive broadcast problem.
tasks.altitude: Less mechanical log comparison; accountability for corrections and compliance remains unchanged.

reach.task: Reconcile transmission records with program logs

evidence.claim: Mediagenix Scheduling Automation checks rights, repeat limits and content rules when building playlists; this supports a native-rule capability check, not proof of completed-log compliance.
The proposed completed-log comparison and hours are unmeasured model scenarios.

assumptions: Boundary is retrospective completed-log accuracy and conformance review, excluding creating the schedule, live timing oversight, legal rule interpretation and regulatory submission. Shared comparisons must have one owner across tasks.

OTHER means broadcast scheduling and logging software. Existing transmission systems produce program identifier, actual start, end, timezone, channel and event status; existing programme metadata staff produce recorded categories and rights references. Their normal production work is outside this task; additional field upkeep is counted below.

Director produces the checked bundle and rule specification in s1's 30 hours: log version, selected period, rule identifier and version, scope, relevant category field, threshold, denominator, timing tolerance, exclusions and source reference. No free discrepancy code or inferred legal category is assumed.

Missing identifiers, unverified classifications, incomplete logs or unclear rules stop automated conclusions and go to manual investigation in s3. Arithmetic flags discrepancies only; no automatic correction or compliance certificate is issued.

The task's US regulatory wording is adapted to the broadcaster's applicable European and national rules, confirmed by its compliance specialists through existing work. Try native checks first; s3 retains source review, exceptions and correction approval.
unknowns: Applicable jurisdiction and broadcaster rule set
Completeness and reliability of recorded programme categories
research_questions: Do configured checks find known timing and rule-total discrepancies without treating missing categories as compliant?

already_counted.description: Capture checking rules, investigate exceptions and approve exact log corrections

incremental.description: Maintain rules and retest log mappings

approvals.approved_version: Exact corrected log version, source snapshot, resolved discrepancies and qualified conformance assessment; changes void acceptance

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=75, gross=25; subtract 7 focal upkeep for central net=18. Range assumes only explicit stable checks run automatically and ambiguous classification stays manual; 4 other-role hours are outside the focal denominator.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Read news and prepare public service and promotional announcement material
Read or record announcements and perform other on-air duties

tasks.design: Keep editorial preparation in {DOCS} and human delivery through {OTHER}, the broadcast recording and transmission equipment. No synthetic voice, automatic publication or reduction in on-air performance time is proposed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Delivery depends on audience context, voice and real-time editorial judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing production and transmission equipment already supports the work.
tasks.still_hard: A director must handle tone, pronunciation, timing and unexpected live developments.
tasks.human_edge: The speaker communicates meaning and takes responsibility for what the audience hears.
tasks.altitude: Preparation, on-air duties and editorial responsibility remain unchanged.

reach.task: Deliver announcements clearly under time constraints
reach.learn: Voice delivery and live editorial judgement

evidence.claim: Human announcement delivery includes performance and contextual judgement; no task saving is claimed.

assumptions: Boundary is the director's preparation and performance, excluding separate newsroom reporting, scheduling, technical transmission operation and marketing campaign design.

News editors or announcement originators produce source material through unchanged work; the director reads and verifies it within s1. The director produces the delivered words in s2 with full retained time; no free structured script or automatic release flag is assumed.
Existing editorial clearance and technical controls remain outside this proposal and are not bypassed. No new formal approval workflow is invented for live human speech.
Keep current native records and equipment. No new system or maintenance requirement means zero incremental upkeep.
unknowns: Which duties are live and which are recorded
How editorial clearance is handled for each announcement type
research_questions: Are existing editorial and technical responsibilities clear for live and recorded material?

already_counted.description: Prepare material and deliver the human performance

incremental.description: No changed process or new upkeep

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0 and incremental upkeep=0. Preparation and performance retain their full time; no transmission runtime is counted as human saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Direct and coordinate personnel preparing broadcast news, sports and programming

tasks.design: Keep direction and coordination human, with existing {PROJECT} records as a reference. The director resolves competing priorities with the staff responsible for preparing news, sport and programming.
tasks.previous_blocker: Coordination requires shared understanding and negotiation under changing conditions.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing native project records already support the conversation; no additional automation is needed.
tasks.still_hard: Editorial priorities and staff capabilities change and cannot be reduced to a fixed dispatch rule.
tasks.human_edge: The director recognises conflicts and secures realistic commitments.
tasks.altitude: Staff direction and decision rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Coordinate technical delivery with editorial teams

evidence.claim: Broadcast staff direction is interpersonal coordination; no separate administrative saving is assumed.

assumptions: Boundary is staff direction itself, excluding log checking, schedule generation, programme quality review and technical execution. Resolve overlapping coordination ownership before team aggregation.
Staff and editors produce progress accounts and priorities through normal work. Director elicits and evaluates them in the retained 100 hours; no free structured progress capture is assumed.
Keep current native records and communication. No new tool or process means zero incremental upkeep.
unknowns: How editorial and technical authority is divided
Which recurring dependencies cause coordination delays
research_questions: Can staff state the current priority, owner and escalation route after coordination discussions?

already_counted.description: Discuss priorities, resolve conflicts and direct broadcast personnel

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0 and incremental upkeep=0. Human direction keeps its full time; no clerical baseline is invented.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Review programming schedules and guidelines and specify timing checks
Compare actual programming starts and durations with the accepted schedule
Monitor and review performances, guideline adherence and timing exceptions and determine responses

tasks.design: Configure a timing comparison view in {OTHER}, the broadcast monitoring system, using accepted schedule versions. The director still watches programming and judges guideline adherence and performance quality, using {DOCS} for the applicable guidance.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeatedly reconciling actual starts and durations distracted from reviewing the programme itself.
tasks.enabler_now: Timestamped transmission events can be compared with a versioned schedule using fixed arithmetic.
tasks.still_hard: Timely programming can still be poor quality or inconsistent with editorial guidelines.
tasks.human_edge: The director recognises meaning, performance quality and appropriate responses to unexpected content.
tasks.altitude: Less timing arithmetic; direct viewing and editorial response remain human.

reach.learn: Signal gaps, clock conventions and event provenance

evidence.claim: Comparing timestamped events with a versioned schedule is deterministic; quality and guideline interpretation remain judgement. The time scenario is unmeasured.

assumptions: Boundary is ongoing programme monitoring and immediate timing review, excluding retrospective completed-log conformance checks. The same comparison action must not earn savings in both tasks.

Schedulers produce accepted programme identifiers, channel, planned start, planned duration and schedule version through normal planning; transmission systems produce actual starts, ends, channel, programme identifiers and timezone during normal operation, after s1 and before the relevant s2 comparison.

Director creates monitoring specification in s1's 30 hours: schedule version, channel, identifiers, timing tolerance, clock convention and explicit exceptions. No structured quality or guideline-compliance flag is supplied to the machine.

Missing or unmatched events and changed schedules are marked unknown and checked manually in s3. Its 50 hours retain watching, quality judgement, guideline assessment, timing exceptions and response decisions. Additional source-field upkeep is counted below.
Try native monitoring views first; no automatic programme changes, broadcasting decisions or quality scores are proposed.
unknowns: Whether event identifiers match the accepted schedule
How much manual timing comparison is distinct from retrospective log checks
research_questions: Does the view surface timing departures and missing events while leaving quality review unchanged?

already_counted.description: Capture monitoring rules and review programmes and exceptions

incremental.description: Maintain timing mappings and retest schedule changes

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=80, gross=20; subtract 8 focal upkeep for central net=12. Range assumes imperfect event matches and frequent manual exceptions. Three other-role upkeep hours are recorded outside the focal denominator; viewing and editorial judgement do not shrink.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The director can spend less time on explicit timing and log comparisons while retaining staff direction, quality review and on-air responsibility.
reach: Reconcile transmission evidence with broadcast technicians
Coordinate practical delivery with media technical directors
skills_to_grow: Specify explicit log and timing checks

role.ambitious_version: Use traceable broadcast evidence to support editorial oversight while keeping performance and programming decisions human.
